# Generate a Makefile instead of analyzing (`--makefile`)

`--makefile` writes the analyzer commands into `OUTPUT_DIR/Makefile` without
running them. You can then run the analysis with `make`, for example on
another machine or under a build system that controls parallelism.

## Create the Makefile ✅

```sh
CodeChecker analyze compile_commands.json -o reports --makefile
```

```
[INFO] - Done.
```

`reports/` now has `Makefile`, `metadata.json`, `compile_cmd.json`,
`compiler_info.json`, `unique_compile_commands.json`, `conf/` and `fixit/`,
but no results yet.

```make
#
# Autogenerated by CodeChecker v6.30.0.
#
# DO NOT EDIT UNLESS YOU ARE SURE THAT YOU KNOW WHAT YOU ARE DOING.
#

export PATH := /path/to/CodeChecker/bin:...:${PATH}
export PYTHONPATH := /path/to/CodeChecker/lib/python3

# Default target to run all analysis.
default: all

# Target to run only 'clangsa' analysis.
all: all_clangsa

# Target to run only 'clangtidy' analysis.
all: all_clangtidy

7c4c04e7a36437427f489d356ff0a853:
	@echo "[`date +'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'`] - clangsa analyze ~/demo/main.c."
	...
```

There is one target per analyzer action, and `all_clangsa` / `all_clangtidy`
group targets.

## Run it ✅

```sh
make -f reports/Makefile -j2
make -f reports/Makefile -i       # keep going when an analysis fails
make -f reports/Makefile all_clangsa
```

The result files appear in `reports/` and can be read with `CodeChecker parse`.

⚠️ The clang-tidy result files from the Makefile have different names than
the ones `analyze` writes (`main.c_clang-tidy_3b59...` instead of
`main.c_clang-tidy_681d...`). `parse --status` then lists clang-tidy under
"Missing analysis results", but `parse` still prints the clang-tidy reports.
For files without findings, no clang-tidy result file is written.
